<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.16</span> Derivation of the geodesic equation (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/length-geodesics.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Length_Geodesics">7.2</a>)</h1></header>
<p><strong>Setting.</strong> As in Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Metric">7</a>: <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is smooth with constant sign <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma = \pm 1\)</span> on <span class="math inline">\([a,b]\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\gamma([a,b]) \subseteq \mathcal{U}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_\mathcal{U} = \mathscr{X} \circ \gamma\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(s_\gamma\)</span> is smooth and positive on <span class="math inline">\([a,b]\)</span>. The chart representative of the Lagrangian is <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \mathscr{X}(p) ; x_p \big) = \sqrt{\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_{kl}(p) \, x^k_p \, x^l_p}\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\((\partial_m g_{ij})(p) = \partial_m \left[ g_{ij} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right]\big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big)\)</span>. By Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="proof-euler-lagrange.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_proof_Euler_Lagrange">B.14</a>, <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is a geodesic if and only if, for <span class="math inline">\(m = 1, \dots, d\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) \Big]
    - (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) = 0 .
\]</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p><strong>Statement.</strong> <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is a geodesic if and only if, on <span class="math inline">\([a,b]\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
    + \frac{1}{2} \Big( (g^{-1})^{km} \big( \partial_i g_{mj} + \partial_j g_{mi} - \partial_m g_{ij} \big) \Big)\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \,
    \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
    = \frac{s_\gamma'(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} \, \dot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) .
\]</span> Every geodesic admits a constant-speed parametrization, for which the right-hand side vanishes and the geodesic equation (<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/length-geodesics.html#eq_geodesic" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_geodesic">7.1</a>) follows.</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p><strong>Proof.</strong></p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em>Partial derivatives of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\)</span>.</em> Using <span class="math inline">\(\partial \sqrt{f} = \partial f / (2 \sqrt{f})\)</span>, in the velocity slots (<span class="math inline">\(\partial x^i_p / \partial x^m_p = \delta^i_m\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(g_{ij} = g_{ji}\)</span>) and in the position slots (only <span class="math inline">\(g_{ij}\)</span> depends on them):  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}
            &amp;= \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, \frac{g_{ij}(p) \big( \delta^i_m \, x^j_p + x^i_p \, \delta^j_m \big)}{2 \sqrt{\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_{kl}(p) \, x^k_p \, x^l_p}}
            = \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, \frac{g_{mj}(p) \, x^j_p}{\sqrt{\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_{kl}(p) \, x^k_p \, x^l_p}} , \\
            \partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}
            &amp;= \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, \frac{(\partial_m g_{ij})(p) \, x^i_p \, x^j_p}{2 \sqrt{\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_{kl}(p) \, x^k_p \, x^l_p}} .
        \end{align*}</span>  On the curve, <span class="math inline">\(p = \gamma(\lambda)\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(x^i_p = \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} = s_\gamma(\lambda)\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big)
            &amp;= \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, \frac{g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} , \\
            (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big)
            &amp;= \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, \frac{(\partial_m g_{ij})\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)}{2 \, s_\gamma(\lambda)} .
        \end{align*}</span></p></li>
<li><p><em>Euler–Lagrange equations</em>, after inserting step 1 and multiplying by <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, s_\gamma(\lambda) \neq 0\)</span> (<span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma^2 = 1\)</span>):  <span class="math display">\[
            s_\gamma(\lambda) \, \frac{d}{d\lambda} \left( \frac{g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} \right)
            - \frac{1}{2} (\partial_m g_{ij})\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) = 0 .
        \]</span></p></li>
<li><p><em>Expansion of the <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span>-derivative.</em> By the quotient rule, and since <span class="math inline">\((g_{mj} \circ \gamma)'(\lambda) = v_{\gamma(\lambda)}(g_{mj}) = \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, (\partial_i g_{mj})\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big)\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            s_\gamma(\lambda) \, \frac{d}{d\lambda} \left( \frac{g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} \right)
            &amp;= \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big( g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \Big)
            - \frac{s_\gamma'(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} \, g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \\
            &amp;= (\partial_i g_{mj})\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            + g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \ddot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \\
            &amp;\quad - \frac{s_\gamma'(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} \, g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ,
        \end{align*}</span>  so step 2 reads  <span class="math display">\[
            g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \ddot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            + \Big( \partial_i g_{mj} - \frac{1}{2} \partial_m g_{ij} \Big)\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            = \frac{s_\gamma'(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} \, g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) .
        \]</span></p></li>
<li><p><em>Symmetrization.</em> Renaming the summed indices <span class="math inline">\(i \leftrightarrow j\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\[
            (\partial_i g_{mj})\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            = (\partial_j g_{mi})\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda),
        \]</span>  so that, taking half of each,  <span class="math display">\[
            (\partial_i g_{mj})\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            = \frac{1}{2} \big( \partial_i g_{mj} + \partial_j g_{mi} \big)\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ,
        \]</span>  and step 3 becomes  <span class="math display">\[
            g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \ddot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            + \frac{1}{2} \big( \partial_i g_{mj} + \partial_j g_{mi} - \partial_m g_{ij} \big)\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda)
            = \frac{s_\gamma'(\lambda)}{s_\gamma(\lambda)} \, g_{mj}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) .
        \]</span></p></li>
<li><p><em>Isolation of <span class="math inline">\(\ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U}\)</span>.</em> Multiplying by <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{km}\big( \gamma(\lambda) \big)\)</span>, summing over <span class="math inline">\(m\)</span>, and using <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{km} \, g_{mj} = \delta^k_j\)</span>, we obtain the equation of the statement. All steps are reversible (<span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, s_\gamma \neq 0\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(g^{-1}\)</span> invertible), so <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is a geodesic if and only if it holds on <span class="math inline">\([a,b]\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Constant speed.</em> Being a geodesic does not depend on the parametrization: for <span class="math inline">\(\delta \coloneqq \gamma \circ \sigma\)</span>, the variations of <span class="math inline">\(\delta\)</span> are the <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \circ \sigma\)</span>, as <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \circ \sigma = \gamma_\mathcal{U} \circ \sigma + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \circ \sigma\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(L_{\sigma^{-1}([a,b])}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \circ \sigma] = L_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}]\)</span> (Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="proof-length-reparametrization.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_proof_length_reparametrization">B.13</a>), so both derivatives at <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0\)</span> coincide. Choosing <span class="math inline">\(\sigma^{-1}(\lambda) \coloneqq \int_a^\lambda s_\gamma = L_{[a,\lambda]}[\gamma]\)</span>, a diffeomorphism since <span class="math inline">\(s_\gamma &gt; 0\)</span>, gives <span class="math inline">\(s_\delta = \sigma' \, (s_\gamma \circ \sigma) \equiv 1\)</span>. For constant speed, <span class="math inline">\(s_\gamma' = 0\)</span>, the right-hand side of the statement vanishes and (<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/length-geodesics.html#eq_geodesic" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_geodesic">7.1</a>) follows. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p></li>
</ol>
